quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: When passing parked cars, which part of the lane should you use?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane
Either the left or right portion of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing parked cars. This keeps you away from opening doors, people stepping out between cars, and cars pulling out of spaces.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid hitting an object in the road, you should:
questions.explanation: Slow down as much as you can before hitting the object. Keep your motorcycle upright, rise slightly off the seat, and roll the throttle slightly to lighten the front end just before impact.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT affect blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How fast the alcohol is consumed
How often the drinker consumes alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the drinker consumes alcohol
questions.explanation: Three things affect blood alcohol content: how much alcohol is consumed, how fast it is consumed, and the drinker's body weight. How often someone drinks does not affect their BAC. It is illegal and dangerous to drive while under the influence of alcohol.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs show traffic rules and regulations, such as speed limits. They are white with black lettering. You must follow all rules posted on these signs.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time to a hazard, you should:

options.text: Always ride under the speed limit.

questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like school zones or construction zones, cover the clutch and both brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to a hazard.

questions.question: When riding in a traffic lane, a motorcycle operator should:

options.text: Always ride in the same part of the lane.
Change lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Always ride in the center of the lane.
Always ride in the left part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: When riding at night, the minimum following distance should be:
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to see and judge distances. Keep a following distance of at least three seconds. It takes longer to realize the vehicle ahead has stopped and longer to slow down or stop to avoid a crash.

questions.question: For an eye or face shield to work properly, it must:

options.text: Not allow for eyeglasses to fit underneath.
Restrict your vision to the sides.

questions.explanation: An effective eye or face shield must be scratch-free, resist penetration, allow clear side vision, fasten securely, allow air to pass through to prevent fogging, and fit over eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: To prevent fatigue on a long ride, do all of the following EXCEPT:

options.text: Limit the distance traveled in a day.

questions.explanation: To reduce fatigue, dress to protect against harsh weather like wind and rain. Limit riding to about six hours per day and take a break at least every two hours. Do not use artificial stimulants, as extreme fatigue may occur when they wear off.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should position themselves:

options.text: In the front of the group.
At the tail end of the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This keeps them from having to chase the group and allows experienced riders to watch them from behind.

questions.question: If you ride a three-wheeled motorcycle or ride with a sidecar, do not ride too far to the right of your lane because:

options.text: Other drivers may not see you.
You will not be able to pass other vehicles as easily.
Other drivers may try to share your lane.
You may run off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may run off the road.
questions.explanation: A sidecar is on the right side of a motorcycle. Riding too far to the right can make the sidecar run off the road. On a three-wheeled motorcycle, the rear right wheel may also leave the road if you get too close to the right edge.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what is the best riding formation?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding. Switch to a single-file line when turning, riding in a curve, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They warn drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: If a dog chases your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest.
Approach the dog slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the dog slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog chases you, slow down and approach it gradually. Then accelerate and leave it behind. If a larger animal blocks your path, brake and prepare to stop.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you from behind, you should:

options.text: Stay in the center portion of the lane.
Stay in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed from behind or by an oncoming vehicle, stay in the center of your lane. Moving closer to the passing vehicle creates danger.

questions.question: To swerve correctly, you should:

options.text: Press the handle grip in the direction you plan to swerve.
Press the handle grip in the direction opposite of where you plan to swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handle grip in the direction you plan to swerve.
questions.explanation: To swerve and avoid a hazard, press the handle grip in the direction you want to go. To swerve left, press the left handle grip, then the right to straighten out. To swerve right, press the right handle grip, then the left.

questions.question: When applying the front brake, you should:

options.text: Apply the lever by squeezing firmly and progressively.
Grab at the brake with only two fingers.
Press down on the brake lever with your foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the lever by squeezing firmly and progressively.
questions.explanation: To apply the front brake, squeeze the brake lever firmly and smoothly with all four fingers. Apply gradually more force as needed.

questions.question: When stopping, it is best to:

options.text: Grab at the front brake lever.
Keep your knees against the gas tank and keep your eyes up.
Apply increasing pressure to the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank and keep your eyes up.
questions.explanation: For the best straight-line braking, apply the brakes smoothly and firmly. Press the front brake harder as weight shifts forward and more traction becomes available. Reduce pressure on the rear brake as you continue. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your eyes up to stay in a straight line.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riders rarely hear a tire going flat. You will notice a change in how the motorcycle handles instead.

questions.question: When entering a turn, a rider should:

options.text: Move their shoulders to match the angle of the turn.
Sit up as high as possible.

questions.explanation: Before entering a turn, reduce your speed by closing the throttle and applying both brakes if needed.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheel motorcycle in a group, what formation should you use?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation works well for two-wheeled motorcycles. However, three-wheeled motorcycles are too wide for this formation. Groups of three-wheeled motorcycles should travel in a single-file line.

questions.question: When carrying a heavy load on your motorcycle, what should you adjust?
questions.explanation: Before riding with a heavy load, adjust your tire pressure, spring pre-load, air shocks, and dampers to match the extra weight you are carrying.

questions.question: A rider wearing a helmet is _______ more likely to survive a crash than a rider without a helmet.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders who wear helmets. This is true regardless of speed.

questions.question: How can a motorcyclist prevent other vehicles from sharing their lane?

options.text: Ride in the left portion of a lane.
Ride in the center portion of a lane.
Give dirty looks if another driver moves into your lane.
Ride in a zigzag pattern to fill up the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of a lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center portion of your lane to discourage other drivers from trying to squeeze in next to you.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, which action should you NOT take?

options.text: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
Use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, use both brakes when slowing or stopping, reduce your speed, and avoid sudden moves. Watch for oil, dirt, gravel, shaded areas, and bridges, as these are more likely to be slippery.
